    52→// hookInputData contains parsed hook input and session identifiers.
    53→type hookInputData struct {
    54→	agent           agent.Agent
    55→	input           *agent.HookInput
    56→	modelSessionID  string
    57→	entireSessionID string
    58→}
    59→
    60→// parseAndLogHookInput parses the hook input and sets up logging context.
    61→func parseAndLogHookInput() (*hookInputData, error) {
    62→	// Get the agent from the hook command context (e.g., "entire hooks claude-code ...")
    63→	ag, err := GetCurrentHookAgent()
    64→	if err != nil {
    65→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
    66→	}
    67→
    68→	// Parse hook input using agent interface
    69→	input, err := ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookUserPromptSubmit, os.Stdin)
    70→	if err != nil {
    71→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook input: %w", err)
    72→	}
    73→
    74→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"), ag.Name())
    75→	logging.Info(logCtx, "user-prompt-submit",
    76→		slog.String("hook", "user-prompt-submit"),
    77→		slog.String("hook_type", "agent"),
    78→		slog.String("model_session_id", input.SessionID),
    79→		slog.String("transcript_path", input.SessionRef),
    80→	)
    81→
    82→	modelSessionID := input.SessionID
    83→	if modelSessionID == "" {
    84→		modelSessionID = unknownSessionID
    85→	}
    86→
    87→	// Get the Entire session ID, preferring the persisted value to handle midnight boundary
    88→	entireSessionID := currentSessionIDWithFallback(modelSessionID)
    89→
    90→	return &hookInputData{
    91→		agent:           ag,
    92→		input:           input,
    93→		modelSessionID:  modelSessionID,
    94→		entireSessionID: entireSessionID,
    95→	}, nil
    96→}
    97→
    98→// checkConcurrentSessions checks for concurrent session conflicts and shows warnings if needed.
    99→// Returns true if the hook should be skipped due to an unresolved conflict.
   100→func checkConcurrentSessions(ag agent.Agent, entireSessionID string) (bool, error) {
   101→	// Check if warnings are disabled via settings
   102→	if IsMultiSessionWarningDisabled() {
   103→		return false, nil
   104→	}
   105→
   106→	strat := GetStrategy()
   107→
   108→	concurrentChecker, ok := strat.(strategy.ConcurrentSessionChecker)
   109→	if !ok {
   110→		return false, nil // Strategy doesn't support concurrent checks
   111→	}
   112→
   113→	// Check if this session already acknowledged the warning
   114→	existingState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(entireSessionID)
   115→	warningAlreadyShown := loadErr == nil && existingState != nil && existingState.ConcurrentWarningShown
   116→
   117→	// Check for other active sessions with checkpoints (on current HEAD)
   118→	otherSession, checkErr := concurrentChecker.HasOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(entireSessionID)
   119→	hasConflict := checkErr == nil && otherSession != nil
   120→
   121→	if warningAlreadyShown {
   122→		if hasConflict {
   123→			// Warning was shown and conflict still exists - skip hooks
   124→			return true, nil
   125→		}
   126→		// Warning was shown but conflict is resolved (e.g., user committed)
   127→		// Clear the flag and proceed normally
   128→		if existingState != nil {
   129→			existingState.ConcurrentWarningShown = false
   130→			if saveErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(existingState); saveErr != nil {
   131→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to clear concurrent warning flag: %v\n", saveErr)
   132→			}
   133→		}
   134→		return false, nil
   135→	}
   136→
   137→	if hasConflict {
   138→		// First time seeing conflict - show warning
   139→		// Include BaseCommit and WorktreePath so session state is complete for condensation
   140→		repo, err := strategy.OpenRepository()
   141→		if err != nil {
   142→			// Output user-friendly error message via hook response
   143→			if outputErr := outputHookResponse(false, fmt.Sprintf("Failed to open git repository: %v\n\nPlease ensure you're in a git repository and try again.", err)); outputErr != nil {
   144→				return false, outputErr
   145→			}
   146→			return true, nil // Skip hook after outputting response
   147→		}
   148→		head, err := repo.Head()
   149→		if err != nil {
   150→			// Output user-friendly error message via hook response
   151→			if outputErr := outputHookResponse(false, fmt.Sprintf("Failed to get git HEAD: %v\n\nPlease ensure the repository has at least one commit.", err)); outputErr != nil {
   152→				return false, outputErr
   153→			}
   154→			return true, nil // Skip hook after outputting response
   155→		}
   156→		worktreePath, err := strategy.GetWorktreePath()
   157→		if err != nil {
   158→			// Non-fatal: continue without worktree path
   159→			worktreePath = ""
   160→		}
   161→		worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
   162→		if err != nil {
   163→			// Non-fatal: continue with empty worktree ID (main worktree)
   164→			worktreeID = ""
   165→		}
   166→		agentType := ag.Type()
   167→		newState := &strategy.SessionState{
   168→			SessionID:              entireSessionID,
   169→			BaseCommit:             head.Hash().String(),
   170→			WorktreePath:           worktreePath,
   171→			WorktreeID:             worktreeID,
   172→			ConcurrentWarningShown: true,
   173→			StartedAt:              time.Now(),
   174→			AgentType:              agentType,
   175→		}
   176→		if saveErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(newState); saveErr != nil {
   177→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to save session state: %v\n", saveErr)
   178→		}
   179→
   180→		// Get resume command for the other session using the CONFLICTING session's agent type.
   181→		// If the conflicting session is from a different agent (e.g., Gemini when we're Claude),
   182→		// use that agent's resume command format. Otherwise, use our own format (backward compatible).
   183→		var resumeCmd string
   184→		if otherSession.AgentType != "" && otherSession.AgentType != agentType {
   185→			// Different agent type - look up the conflicting agent
   186→			if conflictingAgent, agentErr := agent.GetByAgentType(otherSession.AgentType); agentErr == nil {
   187→				resumeCmd = conflictingAgent.FormatResumeCommand(conflictingAgent.ExtractAgentSessionID(otherSession.SessionID))
   188→			}
   189→		}
   190→		// Fall back to current agent if same type or couldn't get the conflicting agent
   191→		if resumeCmd == "" {
   192→			resumeCmd = ag.FormatResumeCommand(ag.ExtractAgentSessionID(otherSession.SessionID))
   193→		}
   194→
   195→		// Try to read the other session's initial prompt
   196→		otherPrompt := strategy.ReadSessionPromptFromShadow(repo, otherSession.BaseCommit, otherSession.WorktreeID, otherSession.SessionID)
   197→
   198→		// Build message with other session's prompt if available
   199→		var message string
   200→		suppressHint := "\n\nTo suppress this warning in future sessions, run:\n  entire enable --disable-multisession-warning"
   201→		if otherPrompt != "" {
   202→			message = fmt.Sprintf("Another session is active: \"%s\"\n\nYou can continue here, but checkpoints from both sessions will be interleaved.\n\nTo resume the other session instead, exit Claude and run: %s%s\n\nPress the up arrow key to get your prompt back.", otherPrompt, resumeCmd, suppressHint)
   203→		} else {
   204→			message = "Another session is active with uncommitted changes. You can continue here, but checkpoints from both sessions will be interleaved.\n\nTo resume the other session instead, exit Claude and run: " + resumeCmd + suppressHint + "\n\nPress the up arrow key to get your prompt back."
   205→		}
   206→
   207→		// Output blocking JSON response - warn about concurrent sessions but allow continuation
   208→		// Both sessions will capture checkpoints, which will be interleaved on the shadow branch
   209→		if err := outputHookResponse(false, message); err != nil {
   210→			return false, err // Failed to output response
   211→		}
   212→		// Block the first prompt to show the warning, but subsequent prompts will proceed
   213→		return true, nil
   214→	}
   215→
   216→	return false, nil
   217→}

   219→// handleSessionStartCommon is the shared implementation for session start hooks.
   220→// Used by both Claude Code and Gemini CLI handlers.
   221→func handleSessionStartCommon() error {
   222→	ag, err := GetCurrentHookAgent()

   224→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)

   260→// handleSessionInitErrors handles session initialization errors and provides user-friendly messages.
   261→func handleSessionInitErrors(ag agent.Agent, initErr error) error {
   262→	// Check for session ID conflict error (shadow branch has different session)
   263→	var sessionConflictErr *strategy.SessionIDConflictError
   264→	if errors.As(initErr, &sessionConflictErr) {
   265→		// If multi-session warnings are disabled, skip this error silently
   266→		// The user has explicitly opted to work with multiple concurrent sessions
   267→		if IsMultiSessionWarningDisabled() {
   268→			return nil
   269→		}
   270→
   271→		// Check if EITHER session has the concurrent warning shown
   272→		// If so, the user was already warned and chose to continue - allow concurrent sessions
   273→		existingState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionConflictErr.ExistingSession)
   274→		newState, newLoadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionConflictErr.NewSession)
   275→		if (loadErr == nil && existingState != nil && existingState.ConcurrentWarningShown) ||
   276→			(newLoadErr == nil && newState != nil && newState.ConcurrentWarningShown) {
   277→			// At least one session was warned - allow concurrent operation
   278→			return nil
   279→		}
   280→		// Try to get the conflicting session's agent type from its state file
   281→		// If it's a different agent type, use that agent's resume command format
   282→		var resumeCmd string
   283→		if loadErr == nil && existingState != nil && existingState.AgentType != "" {
   284→			if conflictingAgent, agentErr := agent.GetByAgentType(existingState.AgentType); agentErr == nil {
   285→				resumeCmd = conflictingAgent.FormatResumeCommand(conflictingAgent.ExtractAgentSessionID(sessionConflictErr.ExistingSession))
   286→			}
   287→		}
   288→		// Fall back to current agent if we couldn't get the conflicting agent
   289→		if resumeCmd == "" {
   290→			resumeCmd = ag.FormatResumeCommand(ag.ExtractAgentSessionID(sessionConflictErr.ExistingSession))
   291→		}
   292→		message := fmt.Sprintf(
   293→			"Warning: Session ID conflict detected!\n\n"+
   294→				"Shadow branch: %s\n"+
   295→				"Existing session: %s\n"+
   296→				"New session: %s\n\n"+
   297→				"The shadow branch already has checkpoints from a different session.\n"+
   298→				"Starting a new session would orphan the existing work.\n\n"+
   299→				"Options:\n"+
   300→				"1. Commit your changes (git commit) to create a new base commit\n"+
   301→				"2. Run 'entire reset' to discard the shadow branch and start fresh\n"+
   302→				"3. Resume the existing session: %s\n\n"+
   303→				"To suppress this warning in future sessions, run:\n"+
   304→				"  entire enable --disable-multisession-warning",
   305→			sessionConflictErr.ShadowBranch,
   306→			sessionConflictErr.ExistingSession,
   307→			sessionConflictErr.NewSession,
   308→			resumeCmd,
   309→		)
   310→		// Output blocking JSON response - user must resolve conflict before continuing
   311→		if err := outputHookResponse(false, message); err != nil {
   312→			return err
   313→		}
   314→		// Return nil so hook exits cleanly (status 0), not with error status
   315→		return nil
   316→	}
   317→
   318→	// Unknown error type
   319→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to initialize session state: %v\n", initErr)
   320→	return nil
   321→}

   323→// captureInitialState captures the initial state on user prompt submit.
   324→func captureInitialState() error {

   326→	hookData, err := parseAndLogHookInput()
   327→	if err != nil {
   328→		return err
   329→	}
   330→
   331→	// UNLESS the situation has changed (e.g., user committed, so no more conflict).
   332→	skipHook, err := checkConcurrentSessions(hookData.agent, hookData.entireSessionID)
   333→	if err != nil {
   334→		return err
   335→	}
   336→	if skipHook {
   337→		return nil
   338→	}
   339→
   340→	// CLI captures state directly (including transcript position)
   341→	if err := CapturePrePromptState(hookData.entireSessionID, hookData.input.SessionRef); err != nil {
   342→		return err
   343→	}
   344→
   345→	// If strategy implements SessionInitializer, call it to initialize session state
   346→	strat := GetStrategy()
   347→	if initializer, ok := strat.(strategy.SessionInitializer); ok {
   348→		agentType := hookData.agent.Type()
   349→		if initErr := initializer.InitializeSession(hookData.entireSessionID, agentType, hookData.input.SessionRef); initErr != nil {
   350→			if err := handleSessionInitErrors(hookData.agent, initErr); err != nil {
   351→				return err
   352→			}
   353→		}
   354→	}
   355→
   356→	return nil
   357→}

   359→// commitWithMetadata commits the session changes with metadata.
   360→func commitWithMetadata() error {
   361→	hookStart := time.Now()
   362→	defer func() {
   363→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] stop hook total: %v\n", time.Since(hookStart))
   364→	}()
   365→
   366→	// Skip on default branch for strategies that don't allow it
   367→	if skip, branchName := ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranchForStrategy(); skip {
   368→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Entire: skipping on branch '%s' - create a feature branch to use Entire tracking\n", branchName)
   369→		return nil // Don't fail the hook, just skip
   370→	}
   371→
   372→	// Get the agent for hook input parsing and session ID transformation
   373→	ag, err := GetCurrentHookAgent()
   374→	if err != nil {
   375→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   376→	}
   377→
   378→	// Parse hook input using agent interface
   379→	input, err := ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookStop, os.Stdin)
   380→	if err != nil {
   381→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook input: %w", err)
   382→	}
   383→
   384→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"), ag.Name())
   385→	logging.Info(logCtx, "stop",
   386→		slog.String("hook", "stop"),
   387→		slog.String("hook_type", "agent"),
   388→		slog.String("model_session_id", input.SessionID),
   389→		slog.String("transcript_path", input.SessionRef),
   390→	)
   391→
   392→	modelSessionID := input.SessionID
   393→	if modelSessionID == "" {
   394→		modelSessionID = unknownSessionID
   395→	}
   396→
   397→	// Get the Entire session ID, preferring the persisted value to handle midnight boundary
   398→	entireSessionID := currentSessionIDWithFallback(modelSessionID)
   399→
   400→	transcriptPath := input.SessionRef
   401→	if transcriptPath == "" || !fileExists(transcriptPath) {
   402→		return fmt.Errorf("transcript file not found or empty: %s", transcriptPath)
   403→	}
   404→
   405→	// Create session metadata folder using the entire session ID (preserves original date on resume)
   406→	// Use AbsPath to ensure we create at repo root, not relative to cwd
   407→	sessionDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromEntireID(entireSessionID)
   408→	sessionDirAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(sessionDir)
   409→	if err != nil {
   410→		sessionDirAbs = sessionDir // Fallback to relative
   411→	}
   412→	if err := os.MkdirAll(sessionDirAbs, 0o750); err != nil {
   413→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
   414→	}
   415→
   416→	// Copy transcript
   417→	copyStart := time.Now()
   418→	logFile := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName)
   419→	if err := copyFile(transcriptPath, logFile); err != nil {
   420→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to copy transcript: %w", err)
   421→	}
   422→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] copy transcript: %v\n", time.Since(copyStart))
   423→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Copied transcript to: %s\n", sessionDir+"/"+paths.TranscriptFileName)
   424→
   425→	// Load session state to get transcript offset (for strategies that track it)
   426→	// This is used to only parse NEW transcript lines since the last checkpoint
   427→	var transcriptOffset int
   428→	sessionState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(entireSessionID)
   429→	if loadErr != nil {
   430→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state: %v\n", loadErr)
   431→	}
   432→	if sessionState != nil {
   433→		transcriptOffset = sessionState.CondensedTranscriptLines
   434→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session state found: parsing transcript from line %d\n", transcriptOffset)
   435→	}
   436→
   437→	// Parse transcript (optionally from offset for strategies that track transcript position)
   438→	// When transcriptOffset > 0, only parse NEW lines since the last checkpoint
   439→	parseStart := time.Now()
   440→	var transcript []transcriptLine
   441→	var totalLines int
   442→	if transcriptOffset > 0 {
   443→		// Parse only NEW lines since last checkpoint
   444→		transcript, totalLines, err = parseTranscriptFromLine(transcriptPath, transcriptOffset)
   445→		if err != nil {
   446→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript from line %d: %w", transcriptOffset, err)
   447→		}
   448→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Parsed %d new transcript lines (total: %d)\n", len(transcript), totalLines)
   449→	} else {
   450→		// First prompt or no session state - parse entire transcript
   451→		// Use parseTranscriptFromLine with offset 0 to also get totalLines
   452→		transcript, totalLines, err = parseTranscriptFromLine(transcriptPath, 0)
   453→		if err != nil {
   454→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
   455→		}
   456→	}
   457→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] parse transcript: %v\n", time.Since(parseStart))
   458→
   459→	// Extract all prompts since last checkpoint for prompt file
   460→	allPrompts := extractUserPrompts(transcript)
   461→	promptFile := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.PromptFileName)
   462→	promptContent := strings.Join(allPrompts, "\n\n---\n\n")
   463→	if err := os.WriteFile(promptFile, []byte(promptContent), 0o600); err != nil {
   464→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write prompt file: %w", err)
   465→	}
   466→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Extracted %d prompt(s) to: %s\n", len(allPrompts), sessionDir+"/"+paths.PromptFileName)
   467→
   468→	// Extract summary
   469→	summaryFile := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.SummaryFileName)
   470→	summary := extractLastAssistantMessage(transcript)
   471→	if err := os.WriteFile(summaryFile, []byte(summary), 0o600); err != nil {
   472→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write summary file: %w", err)
   473→	}
   474→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Extracted summary to: %s\n", sessionDir+"/"+paths.SummaryFileName)
   475→
   476→	// Get modified files from transcript
   477→	modifiedFiles := extractModifiedFiles(transcript)
   478→
   479→	// Generate commit message from last user prompt
   480→	lastPrompt := ""
   481→	if len(allPrompts) > 0 {
   482→		lastPrompt = allPrompts[len(allPrompts)-1]
   483→	}
   484→	commitMessage := generateCommitMessage(lastPrompt)
   485→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Using commit message: %s\n", commitMessage)
   486→
   487→	// Get repo root for path conversion (not cwd, since Claude may be in a subdirectory)
   488→	// Using cwd would filter out files in sibling directories (paths starting with ..)
   489→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   490→	if err != nil {
   491→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   492→	}
   493→
   494→	// Load pre-prompt state (captured on UserPromptSubmit)
   495→	preState, err := LoadPrePromptState(entireSessionID)
   496→	if err != nil {
   497→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load pre-prompt state: %v\n", err)
   498→	}
   499→	if preState != nil {
   500→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Loaded pre-prompt state: %d pre-existing untracked files\n", len(preState.UntrackedFiles))
   501→	}
   502→
   503→	// Compute new files (files created during session)
   504→	newFilesStart := time.Now()
   505→	newFiles, err := ComputeNewFiles(preState)
   506→	if err != nil {
   507→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to compute new files: %v\n", err)
   508→	}
   509→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] ComputeNewFiles: %v\n", time.Since(newFilesStart))
   510→
   511→	// Compute deleted files (tracked files that were deleted)
   512→	deletedFilesStart := time.Now()
   513→	deletedFiles, err := ComputeDeletedFiles()
   514→	if err != nil {
   515→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to compute deleted files: %v\n", err)
   516→	}
   517→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] ComputeDeletedFiles: %v\n", time.Since(deletedFilesStart))
   518→
   519→	// Filter and normalize all paths (CLI responsibility)
   520→	relModifiedFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(modifiedFiles, repoRoot)
   521→	relNewFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(newFiles, repoRoot)
   522→	relDeletedFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(deletedFiles, repoRoot)
   523→
   524→	// Check if there are any changes to commit
   525→	totalChanges := len(relModifiedFiles) + len(relNewFiles) + len(relDeletedFiles)
   526→	if totalChanges == 0 {
   527→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "No files were modified during this session\n")
   528→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Skipping commit\n")
   529→		// Clean up state even when skipping
   530→		if err := CleanupPrePromptState(entireSessionID); err != nil {
   531→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to cleanup pre-prompt state: %v\n", err)
   532→		}
   533→		return nil
   534→	}
   535→
   536→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Files modified during session (%d):\n", len(relModifiedFiles))
   537→	for _, file := range relModifiedFiles {
   538→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", file)
   539→	}
   540→	if len(relNewFiles) > 0 {
   541→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "New files created (%d):\n", len(relNewFiles))
   542→		for _, file := range relNewFiles {
   543→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  + %s\n", file)
   544→		}
   545→	}
   546→	if len(relDeletedFiles) > 0 {
   547→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Files deleted (%d):\n", len(relDeletedFiles))
   548→		for _, file := range relDeletedFiles {
   549→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", file)
   550→		}
   551→	}
   552→
   553→	// Create context file before saving changes
   554→	contextFile := filepath.Join(sessionDirAbs, paths.ContextFileName)
   555→	if err := createContextFileMinimal(contextFile, commitMessage, entireSessionID, promptFile, summaryFile, transcript); err != nil {
   556→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create context file: %w", err)
   557→	}
   558→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Created context file: %s\n", sessionDir+"/"+paths.ContextFileName)
   559→
   560→	// Get git author from local/global config
   561→	author, err := GetGitAuthor()
   562→	if err != nil {
   563→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get git author: %w", err)
   564→	}
   565→
   566→	// Get the configured strategy
   567→	strat := GetStrategy()
   568→
   569→	// Ensure strategy setup is in place (auto-installs git hook, gitignore, etc. if needed)
   570→	if err := strat.EnsureSetup(); err != nil {
   571→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to ensure strategy setup: %v\n", err)
   572→	}
   573→
   574→	// Get agent type from the currently executing hook agent (authoritative source)
   575→	var agentType agent.AgentType
   576→	if hookAgent, agentErr := GetCurrentHookAgent(); agentErr == nil {
   577→		agentType = hookAgent.Type()
   578→	}
   579→
   580→	// Get transcript position from pre-prompt state (captured at checkpoint start)
   581→	var transcriptIdentifierAtStart string
   582→	var transcriptLinesAtStart int
   583→	if preState != nil {
   584→		transcriptIdentifierAtStart = preState.LastTranscriptIdentifier
   585→		transcriptLinesAtStart = preState.LastTranscriptLineCount
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	// Calculate token usage for this checkpoint (Claude Code specific)
   589→	tokenUsageStart := time.Now()
   590→	var tokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage
   591→	if transcriptPath != "" {
   592→		// Subagents are stored in a subagents/ directory next to the main transcript
   593→		subagentsDir := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath), entireSessionID, "subagents")
   594→		usage, err := claudecode.CalculateTotalTokenUsage(transcriptPath, transcriptLinesAtStart, subagentsDir)
   595→		if err != nil {
   596→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to calculate token usage: %v\n", err)
   597→		} else {
   598→			tokenUsage = usage
   599→		}
   600→	}
   601→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] CalculateTotalTokenUsage: %v\n", time.Since(tokenUsageStart))
   602→
   603→	// Build fully-populated save context and delegate to strategy
   604→	ctx := strategy.SaveContext{
   605→		SessionID:                   entireSessionID,
   606→		ModifiedFiles:               relModifiedFiles,
   607→		NewFiles:                    relNewFiles,
   608→		DeletedFiles:                relDeletedFiles,
   609→		MetadataDir:                 sessionDir,
   610→		MetadataDirAbs:              sessionDirAbs,
   611→		CommitMessage:               commitMessage,
   612→		TranscriptPath:              transcriptPath,
   613→		AuthorName:                  author.Name,
   614→		AuthorEmail:                 author.Email,
   615→		AgentType:                   agentType,
   616→		TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: transcriptIdentifierAtStart,
   617→		TranscriptLinesAtStart:      transcriptLinesAtStart,
   618→		TokenUsage:                  tokenUsage,
   619→	}
   620→
   621→	saveChangesStart := time.Now()
   622→	if err := strat.SaveChanges(ctx); err != nil {
   623→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save changes: %w", err)
   624→	}
   625→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[timing] SaveChanges: %v\n", time.Since(saveChangesStart))
   626→
   627→	// Update session state with new transcript position for strategies that create
   628→	// commits on the active branch (auto-commit strategy). This prevents parsing old transcript
   629→	// lines on subsequent checkpoints.
   630→	// Note: Shadow strategy doesn't create commits on the active branch, so its
   631→	// checkpoints don't "consume" the transcript in the same way. Shadow should
   632→	// continue parsing the full transcript to capture all files touched in the session.
   633→	if strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit {
   634→		// Create session state lazily if it doesn't exist (backward compat for resumed sessions
   635→		// or if InitializeSession was never called/failed)
   636→		if sessionState == nil {
   637→			sessionState = &strategy.SessionState{
   638→				SessionID: entireSessionID,
   639→			}
   640→		}
   641→		sessionState.CondensedTranscriptLines = totalLines
   642→		sessionState.CheckpointCount++
   643→		if updateErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(sessionState); updateErr != nil {
   644→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", updateErr)
   645→		} else {
   646→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Updated session state: transcript position=%d, checkpoint=%d\n",
   647→				totalLines, sessionState.CheckpointCount)
   648→		}
   649→	}
   650→
   651→	// Clean up pre-prompt state (CLI responsibility)
   652→	if err := CleanupPrePromptState(entireSessionID); err != nil {
   653→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to cleanup pre-prompt state: %v\n", err)
   654→	}
   655→
   656→	return nil
   657→}

   659→// handleClaudeCodePostTodo handles the PostToolUse[TodoWrite] hook for subagent checkpoints.
   660→// Creates a checkpoint if we're in a subagent context (active pre-task file exists).
   661→// Skips silently if not in subagent context (main agent).
   662→func handleClaudeCodePostTodo() error {
   663→	input, err := parseSubagentCheckpointHookInput(os.Stdin)
   664→	if err != nil {
   665→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse PostToolUse[TodoWrite] input: %w", err)
   666→	}
   667→
   668→	// Get agent for logging context
   669→	ag, err := GetCurrentHookAgent()
   670→	if err != nil {
   671→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   672→	}
   673→
   674→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"), ag.Name())
   675→	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-todo",
   676→		slog.String("hook", "post-todo"),
   677→		slog.String("hook_type", "subagent"),
   678→		slog.String("model_session_id", input.SessionID),
   679→		slog.String("transcript_path", input.TranscriptPath),
   680→		slog.String("tool_use_id", input.ToolUseID),
   681→	)
   682→
   683→	// Check if we're in a subagent context by looking for an active pre-task file
   684→	taskToolUseID, found := FindActivePreTaskFile()
   685→	if !found {
   686→		// Not in subagent context - this is a main agent TodoWrite, skip
   687→		return nil
   688→	}
   689→
   690→	// Skip on default branch to avoid polluting main/master history
   691→	if skip, branchName := ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranch(); skip {
   692→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Entire: skipping incremental checkpoint on branch '%s'\n", branchName)
   693→		return nil
   694→	}
   695→
   696→	// Detect file changes since last checkpoint
   697→	modified, newFiles, deleted, err := DetectChangedFiles()
   698→	if err != nil {
   699→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to detect changed files: %v\n", err)
   700→		return nil
   701→	}
   702→
   703→	// If no file changes, skip creating a checkpoint
   704→	if len(modified) == 0 && len(newFiles) == 0 && len(deleted) == 0 {
   705→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] No file changes detected, skipping incremental checkpoint\n")
   706→		return nil
   707→	}
   708→
   709→	// Get git author
   710→	author, err := GetGitAuthor()
   711→	if err != nil {
   712→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to get git author: %v\n", err)
   713→		return nil
   714→	}
   715→
   716→	// Get the active strategy
   717→	strat := GetStrategy()
   718→
   719→	// Ensure strategy setup is complete
   720→	if err := strat.EnsureSetup(); err != nil {
   721→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to ensure strategy setup: %v\n", err)
   722→		return nil
   723→	}
   724→
   725→	// Get the session ID from the transcript path or input, then transform to Entire session ID
   726→	sessionID := paths.ExtractSessionIDFromTranscriptPath(input.TranscriptPath)
   727→	if sessionID == "" {
   728→		sessionID = input.SessionID
   729→	}
   730→	entireSessionID := currentSessionIDWithFallback(sessionID)
   731→
   732→	// Get next checkpoint sequence
   733→	seq := GetNextCheckpointSequence(entireSessionID, taskToolUseID)
   734→
   735→	// Extract the todo content from the tool_input.
   736→	// PostToolUse receives the NEW todo list where the just-completed work is
   737→	// marked as "completed". The last completed item is the work that was just done.
   738→	todoContent := ExtractLastCompletedTodoFromToolInput(input.ToolInput)
   739→	if todoContent == "" {
   740→		// No completed items - this is likely the first TodoWrite (planning phase).
   741→		// Check if there are any todos at all to avoid duplicate messages.
   742→		todoCount := CountTodosFromToolInput(input.ToolInput)
   743→		if todoCount > 0 {
   744→			// Use "Planning: N todos" format for the first TodoWrite
   745→			todoContent = fmt.Sprintf("Planning: %d todos", todoCount)
   746→		}
   747→		// If todoCount == 0, todoContent remains empty and FormatIncrementalMessage
   748→		// will fall back to "Checkpoint #N" format
   749→	}
   750→
   751→	// Get agent type from the currently executing hook agent (authoritative source)
   752→	var agentType agent.AgentType
   753→	if hookAgent, agentErr := GetCurrentHookAgent(); agentErr == nil {
   754→		agentType = hookAgent.Type()
   755→	}
   756→
   757→	// Build incremental checkpoint context
   758→	ctx := strategy.TaskCheckpointContext{
   759→		SessionID:           entireSessionID,
   760→		ToolUseID:           taskToolUseID,
   761→		ModifiedFiles:       modified,
   762→		NewFiles:            newFiles,
   763→		DeletedFiles:        deleted,
   764→		TranscriptPath:      input.TranscriptPath,
   765→		AuthorName:          author.Name,
   766→		AuthorEmail:         author.Email,
   767→		IsIncremental:       true,
   768→		IncrementalSequence: seq,
   769→		IncrementalType:     input.ToolName,
   770→		IncrementalData:     input.ToolInput,
   771→		TodoContent:         todoContent,
   772→		AgentType:           agentType,
   773→	}
   774→
   775→	// Save incremental checkpoint
   776→	if err := strat.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx); err != nil {
   777→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to save incremental checkpoint: %v\n", err)
   778→		return nil
   779→	}
   780→
   781→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Created incremental checkpoint #%d for %s (task: %s)\n",
   782→		seq, input.ToolName, taskToolUseID[:min(12, len(taskToolUseID))])
   783→	return nil
   784→}

   828→// handleClaudeCodePostTask handles the PostToolUse[Task] hook
   829→func handleClaudeCodePostTask() error {
   830→	// Skip on default branch for strategies that don't allow it
   831→	if skip, branchName := ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranchForStrategy(); skip {
   832→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Entire: skipping on branch '%s' - create a feature branch to use Entire tracking\n", branchName)

   836→	input, err := parsePostTaskHookInput(os.Stdin)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/alex/.claude/skills/github-pr-review

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 6. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y"` |

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/alex/.claude/skills/github-pr-review

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 6. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y"` |

description: Use when viewing PR review comments, replying to review threads, creating PRs, or changing draft status via gh CLI

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 6. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y"` |

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 6. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Re-fetch comment IDs (if rebased)

**Important:** If you rebased or force-pushed, comment IDs may have changed. Re-fetch the comment threads before replying:

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq '...'
```

### 6. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 7. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

The user is asking about the stop hook and shadow branches. Let me think about what I know from the conversation and CLAUDE.md context.

From the CLAUDE.md documentation, the manual-commit strategy creates shadow branches with the format `entire/<HEAD-commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`. These are used to store checkpoints without modifying the user's active branch.

The stop hook (`entire hooks claude-code stop`) calls `commitWithMetadata()` which eventually calls `SaveChanges()` on the strategy. For manual-commit strategy, this saves checkpoints to the shadow branch.

So yes, the stop hook does create/update shadow branches as part of saving checkpoints.

content.text:
Yes. The manual-commit strategy (default) creates shadow branches named `entire/<HEAD-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` when the stop hook runs.

The flow is:
1. Stop hook calls `commitWithMetadata()`
2. Which calls `strategy.SaveChanges()`
3. Manual-commit strategy builds a git tree in-memory and commits it to the shadow branch

The shadow branch stores:
- Code state (working directory snapshot)
- Metadata in `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/` (transcript, prompts, context)

This is separate from the `entire/sessions` branch which only gets populated when the user commits (via the prepare-commit-msg hook condensation).

Did you have a specific question about the shadow branch behavior?

   288→// mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
   289→func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
   290→	seen := make(map[string]bool)
   291→	for _, f := range existing {
   292→		seen[f] = true
   293→	}
   294→
   295→	for _, list := range fileLists {
   296→		for _, f := range list {
   297→			seen[f] = true
   298→		}
   299→	}
   300→
   301→	result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
   302→	for f := range seen {
   303→		result = append(result, f)
   304→	}
   305→
   306→	// Sort for deterministic output
   307→	sort.Strings(result)
   308→	return result
   309→}

   311→// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   312→// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   313→func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   314→	if incoming == nil {
   315→		return existing
   316→	}
   317→	if existing == nil {
   318→		// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   319→		return &agent.TokenUsage{
   320→			InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   321→			CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   322→			CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   323→			OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   324→			APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   325→			SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   326→		}
   327→	}
   328→
   329→	// Accumulate values
   330→	existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   331→	existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   332→	existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   333→	existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   334→	existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   335→
   336→	// Accumulate subagent tokens if present
   337→	if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   338→		existing.SubagentTokens = accumulateTokenUsage(existing.SubagentTokens, incoming.SubagentTokens)
   339→	}
   340→
   341→	return existing
   342→}

   344→// deleteShadowBranch deletes a shadow branch by name using an existing repo handle.
   345→// Returns nil if the branch doesn't exist (idempotent).
   346→func deleteShadowBranch(repo *git.Repository, branchName string) error {
   347→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   348→
   349→	// Check if reference exists
   350→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   351→	if err != nil {
   352→		// Branch doesn't exist - nothing to delete (idempotent)
   353→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Not an error condition - branch already gone
   354→	}
   355→
   356→	// Delete the reference
   357→	if err := repo.Storer.RemoveReference(ref.Name()); err != nil {
   358→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete branch %s: %w", branchName, err)
   359→	}
   360→
   361→	return nil
   362→}

   222→// Task checkpoints include both code changes and task-specific metadata.
   223→// Returns the commit hash of the created checkpoint.
   224→func (s *GitStore) WriteTemporaryTask(ctx context.Context, opts WriteTemporaryTaskOptions) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   225→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   226→
   227→	// Validate base commit - required for shadow branch naming
   228→	if opts.BaseCommit == "" {
   229→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, errors.New("BaseCommit is required for task checkpoint")
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// Validate identifiers to prevent path traversal and malformed data
   233→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
   234→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("invalid task checkpoint options: %w", err)
   235→	}
   236→	if err := validation.ValidateToolUseID(opts.ToolUseID); err != nil {
   237→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("invalid task checkpoint options: %w", err)
   238→	}
   239→	if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(opts.AgentID); err != nil {
   240→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("invalid task checkpoint options: %w", err)
   241→	}
   242→
   243→	// Get shadow branch name
   244→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(opts.BaseCommit, opts.WorktreeID)
   245→
   246→	// Get or create shadow branch
   247→	parentHash, baseTreeHash, err := s.getOrCreateShadowBranch(shadowBranchName)
   248→	if err != nil {
   249→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get shadow branch: %w", err)
   250→	}
   251→
   252→	// Collect all files to include in the commit
   253→	allFiles := make([]string, 0, len(opts.ModifiedFiles)+len(opts.NewFiles))
   254→	allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.ModifiedFiles...)
   255→	allFiles = append(allFiles, opts.NewFiles...)
   256→
   257→	// Build new tree with code changes (no metadata dir yet)
   258→	newTreeHash, err := s.buildTreeWithChanges(baseTreeHash, allFiles, opts.DeletedFiles, "", "")
   259→	if err != nil {
   260→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to build tree: %w", err)
   261→	}
   262→
   263→	// Add task metadata to tree
   264→	newTreeHash, err = s.addTaskMetadataToTree(newTreeHash, opts)
   265→	if err != nil {
   266→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to add task metadata: %w", err)
   267→	}
   268→
   269→	// Create the commit
   270→	commitHash, err := s.createCommit(newTreeHash, parentHash, opts.CommitMessage, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
   271→	if err != nil {
   272→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create commit: %w", err)
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	// Update shadow branch reference
   276→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   277→	ref := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)
   278→	if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(ref); err != nil {
   279→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to update shadow branch reference: %w", err)
   280→	}
   281→
   282→	return commitHash, nil
   283→}

   285→// addTaskMetadataToTree adds task checkpoint metadata to a git tree.
   286→// When IsIncremental is true, only adds the incremental checkpoint file.
   287→func (s *GitStore) addTaskMetadataToTree(baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash, opts WriteTemporaryTaskOptions) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   288→	// Get base tree and flatten it
   289→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   290→	if err != nil {
   291→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   292→	}
   293→
   294→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   295→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   296→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten tree: %w", err)
   297→	}
   298→
   299→	// Compute metadata paths
   300→	sessionMetadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + opts.SessionID
   301→	taskMetadataDir := sessionMetadataDir + "/tasks/" + opts.ToolUseID
   302→
   303→	if opts.IsIncremental {
   304→		// Incremental checkpoint: only add the checkpoint file
   305→		// Use proper JSON marshaling to handle nil/empty IncrementalData correctly
   306→		incrementalCheckpoint := struct {
   307→			Type      string          `json:"type"`
   308→			ToolUseID string          `json:"tool_use_id"`
   309→			Timestamp time.Time       `json:"timestamp"`
   310→			Data      json.RawMessage `json:"data"`
   311→		}{
   312→			Type:      opts.IncrementalType,
   313→			ToolUseID: opts.ToolUseID,
   314→			Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
   315→			Data:      opts.IncrementalData,
   316→		}
   317→		cpData, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(incrementalCheckpoint, "", "  ")
   318→		if err != nil {
   319→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal incremental checkpoint: %w", err)
   320→		}
   321→
   322→		cpBlobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, cpData)
   323→		if err != nil {
   324→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create incremental checkpoint blob: %w", err)
   325→		}
   326→		cpFilename := fmt.Sprintf("%03d-%s.json", opts.IncrementalSequence, opts.ToolUseID)
   327→		cpPath := taskMetadataDir + "/checkpoints/" + cpFilename
   328→		entries[cpPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   329→			Name: cpPath,
   330→			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   331→			Hash: cpBlobHash,
   332→		}
   333→	} else {
   334→		// Final checkpoint: add transcripts and checkpoint.json
   335→
   336→		// Add session transcript (with chunking support for large transcripts)
   337→		if opts.TranscriptPath != "" {
   338→			if transcriptContent, readErr := os.ReadFile(opts.TranscriptPath); readErr == nil {
   339→				// Detect agent type from content for proper chunking
   340→				agentType := agent.DetectAgentTypeFromContent(transcriptContent)
   341→
   342→				// Chunk if necessary
   343→				chunks, chunkErr := agent.ChunkTranscript(transcriptContent, agentType)
   344→				if chunkErr != nil {
   345→					logging.Warn(context.Background(), "failed to chunk transcript, checkpoint will be saved without transcript",
   346→						slog.String("error", chunkErr.Error()),
   347→						slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
   348→					)
   349→				} else {
   350→					for i, chunk := range chunks {
   351→						chunkPath := sessionMetadataDir + "/" + agent.ChunkFileName(paths.TranscriptFileName, i)
   352→						blobHash, blobErr := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, chunk)
   353→						if blobErr != nil {
   354→							logging.Warn(context.Background(), "failed to create blob for transcript chunk",
   355→								slog.String("error", blobErr.Error()),
   356→								slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
   357→								slog.Int("chunk_index", i),
   358→							)
   359→							continue
   360→						}
   361→						entries[chunkPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   362→							Name: chunkPath,
   363→							Mode: filemode.Regular,
   364→							Hash: blobHash,
   365→						}
   366→					}
   367→				}
   368→			}
   369→		}
   370→
   371→		// Add subagent transcript if available
   372→		if opts.SubagentTranscriptPath != "" && opts.AgentID != "" {
   373→			if agentContent, readErr := os.ReadFile(opts.SubagentTranscriptPath); readErr == nil {
   374→				if blobHash, blobErr := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, agentContent); blobErr == nil {
   375→					agentPath := taskMetadataDir + "/agent-" + opts.AgentID + ".jsonl"
   376→					entries[agentPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   377→						Name: agentPath,
   378→						Mode: filemode.Regular,
   379→						Hash: blobHash,
   380→					}
   381→				}
   382→			}
   383→		}
   384→
   385→		// Add checkpoint.json
   386→		checkpointJSON := fmt.Sprintf(`{
   387→  "session_id": %q,
   388→  "tool_use_id": %q,
   389→  "checkpoint_uuid": %q,
   390→  "agent_id": %q
   391→}`, opts.SessionID, opts.ToolUseID, opts.CheckpointUUID, opts.AgentID)
   392→
   393→		blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(checkpointJSON))
   394→		if err != nil {
   395→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create checkpoint blob: %w", err)
   396→		}
   397→		checkpointPath := taskMetadataDir + "/checkpoint.json"
   398→		entries[checkpointPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   399→			Name: checkpointPath,
   400→			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   401→			Hash: blobHash,
   402→		}
   403→	}
   404→
   405→	// Build new tree from entries
   406→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   407→}

   425→// listCheckpointsForBranch lists checkpoint commits for a specific shadow branch name.
   426→// This is an internal helper used by ListTemporaryCheckpoints, ListCheckpointsForBranch, and ListAllTemporaryCheckpoints.
   427→func (s *GitStore) listCheckpointsForBranch(ctx context.Context, shadowBranchName, sessionID string, limit int) ([]TemporaryCheckpointInfo, error) {
   428→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   429→
   430→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   431→
   432→	ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   433→	if err != nil {
   434→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilerr // No shadow branch is expected case
   435→	}
   436→
   437→	iter, err := s.repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: ref.Hash()})
   438→	if err != nil {
   439→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit log: %w", err)
   440→	}
   441→
   442→	var results []TemporaryCheckpointInfo
   443→	count := 0
   444→
   445→	err = iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   446→		if count >= limit*5 { // Scan more to allow for session filtering
   447→			return errStop
   448→		}
   449→		count++
   450→
   451→		// Verify commit belongs to target session via Entire-Session trailer
   452→		commitSessionID, hasTrailer := trailers.ParseSession(c.Message)
   453→		if !hasTrailer {
   454→			return nil // Skip commits without session trailer
   455→		}
   456→		if sessionID != "" && commitSessionID != sessionID {
   457→			return nil // Skip commits from other sessions
   458→		}
   459→
   460→		// Get first line of message
   461→		message := c.Message
   462→		if idx := strings.Index(message, "\n"); idx > 0 {
   463→			message = message[:idx]
   464→		}
   465→
   466→		info := TemporaryCheckpointInfo{
   467→			CommitHash: c.Hash,
   468→			Message:    message,
   469→			SessionID:  commitSessionID,
   470→			Timestamp:  c.Author.When,
   471→		}
   472→
   473→		// Check for task checkpoint first
   474→		taskMetadataDir, foundTask := trailers.ParseTaskMetadata(c.Message)
   475→		if foundTask {
   476→			info.IsTaskCheckpoint = true
   477→			info.MetadataDir = taskMetadataDir
   478→			info.ToolUseID = extractToolUseIDFromPath(taskMetadataDir)
   479→		} else {
   480→			metadataDir, found := trailers.ParseMetadata(c.Message)
   481→			if found {
   482→				info.MetadataDir = metadataDir
   483→			}
   484→		}
   485→
   486→		results = append(results, info)
   487→
   488→		if len(results) >= limit {
   489→			return errStop
   490→		}
   491→		return nil
   492→	})
   493→
   494→	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errStop) {
   495→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("error iterating commits: %w", err)
   496→	}
   497→
   498→	return results, nil
   499→}

   501→// ListAllTemporaryCheckpoints lists checkpoint commits from ALL shadow branches.
   502→// This is used for checkpoint lookup when the base commit is unknown (e.g., HEAD advanced since session start).
   503→// The sessionID filter, if provided, limits results to commits from that session.
   504→func (s *GitStore) ListAllTemporaryCheckpoints(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, limit int) ([]TemporaryCheckpointInfo, error) {

   507→	// List all shadow branches

   509→	if err != nil {
   510→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list shadow branches: %w", err)
   511→	}
   512→
   513→	var results []TemporaryCheckpointInfo
   514→
   515→	// Iterate through each shadow branch and collect checkpoints
   516→	for _, branch := range branches {

   518→		branchCheckpoints, branchErr := s.listCheckpointsForBranch(ctx, branch.BranchName, sessionID, limit)

   525→			break
   526→		}
   527→	}
   528→
   529→	return results, nil

   532→// extractToolUseIDFromPath extracts the ToolUseID from a task metadata directory path.
   533→// Task metadata dirs have format: .entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/<toolUseID>
   534→func extractToolUseIDFromPath(metadataDir string) string {
   535→	parts := strings.Split(metadataDir, "/")
   536→	if len(parts) >= 2 && parts[len(parts)-2] == "tasks" {
   537→		return parts[len(parts)-1]
   538→	}

   545→// GetTranscriptFromCommit retrieves the transcript from a specific commit's tree.
   546→// This is used for shadow branch checkpoints where the transcript is stored in the commit tree
   547→// rather than on the entire/sessions branch.
   548→// commitHash is the commit to read from, metadataDir is the path within the tree.
   549→// agentType is used for reassembling chunked transcripts in the correct format.
   550→// Handles both chunked and non-chunked transcripts.
   551→func (s *GitStore) GetTranscriptFromCommit(commitHash plumbing.Hash, metadataDir string, agentType agent.AgentType) ([]byte, error) {
   552→	commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(commitHash)
   553→	if err != nil {
   554→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
   555→	}
   556→
   557→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   558→	if err != nil {
   559→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   560→	}
   561→
   562→	// Try to get the metadata subtree for chunk detection
   563→	subTree, subTreeErr := tree.Tree(metadataDir)
   564→	if subTreeErr == nil {
   565→		// Use the helper function that handles chunking
   566→		transcript, err := readTranscriptFromTree(subTree, agentType)
   567→		if err == nil && transcript != nil {
   568→			return transcript, nil
   569→		}
   570→	}
   571→
   572→	// Fall back to direct file access (for backwards compatibility)
   573→	transcriptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
   574→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   575→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   576→		if contentErr == nil {
   577→			return []byte(content), nil
   578→		}
   579→	}
   580→
   581→	transcriptPath = metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy
   582→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   583→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   584→		if contentErr == nil {
   585→			return []byte(content), nil
   586→		}
   587→	}
   588→
   589→	return nil, ErrNoTranscript
   590→}

   603→func (s *GitStore) DeleteShadowBranch(baseCommit, worktreeID string) error {

   605→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)

   612→// ShadowBranchNameForCommit returns the shadow branch name for a base commit hash
   613→// and worktree identifier. The worktree ID should be empty for the main worktree
   614→// or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   615→// Format: entire/<commit[:7]>-<hash(worktreeID)[:6]>
   616→func ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID string) string {
   617→	commitPart := baseCommit
   618→	if len(baseCommit) >= ShadowBranchHashLength {
   619→		commitPart = baseCommit[:ShadowBranchHashLength]
   620→	}
   621→	worktreeHash := HashWorktreeID(worktreeID)
   622→	return ShadowBranchPrefix + commitPart + "-" + worktreeHash
   623→}
   624→
   625→// ParseShadowBranchName extracts the commit prefix and worktree hash from a shadow branch name.
   626→// Input format: "entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>"
   627→// Returns (commitPrefix, worktreeHash, ok). Returns ("", "", false) if not a valid shadow branch.
   628→func ParseShadowBranchName(branchName string) (commitPrefix, worktreeHash string, ok bool) {
   629→	if !strings.HasPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix) {
   630→		return "", "", false
   631→	}
   632→	suffix := strings.TrimPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix)
   633→
   634→	// Find the last dash - everything before is commit prefix, after is worktree hash
   635→	lastDash := strings.LastIndex(suffix, "-")
   636→	if lastDash == -1 || lastDash == 0 || lastDash == len(suffix)-1 {
   637→		// No dash, or dash at start/end - invalid format
   638→		// Could be old format "entire/<commit[:7]>" without worktree hash
   639→		return suffix, "", true // Return as commit prefix with empty worktree hash
   640→	}
   641→
   642→	return suffix[:lastDash], suffix[lastDash+1:], true
   643→}

   645→// getOrCreateShadowBranch gets or creates the shadow branch for checkpoints.
   646→// Returns (parentHash, baseTreeHash, error).
   647→func (s *GitStore) getOrCreateShadowBranch(branchName string) (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   648→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   649→	ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   650→
   651→	if err == nil {
   652→		// Branch exists
   653→		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   654→		if err != nil {
   655→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   656→		}
   657→		return ref.Hash(), commit.TreeHash, nil
   658→	}
   659→
   660→	// Branch doesn't exist, use current HEAD's tree as base
   661→	head, err := s.repo.Head()
   662→	if err != nil {
   663→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   664→	}
   665→
   666→	headCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   667→	if err != nil {
   668→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD commit: %w", err)
   669→	}
   670→
   671→	return plumbing.ZeroHash, headCommit.TreeHash, nil
   672→}

   674→// buildTreeWithChanges builds a git tree with the given changes.
   675→// metadataDir is the relative path for git tree entries, metadataDirAbs is the absolute path
   676→// for filesystem operations (needed when CLI is run from a subdirectory).
   677→func (s *GitStore) buildTreeWithChanges(
   678→	baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash,
   679→	modifiedFiles, deletedFiles []string,
   680→	metadataDir, metadataDirAbs string,
   681→) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   682→	// Get repo root for resolving file paths
   683→	// This is critical because fileExists() and createBlobFromFile() use os.Stat()
   684→	// which resolves relative to CWD. The modifiedFiles are repo-relative paths,
   685→	// so we must resolve them against repo root, not CWD.
   686→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   687→	if err != nil {
   688→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   689→	}
   690→
   691→	// Get the base tree
   692→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   693→	if err != nil {
   694→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   695→	}
   696→
   697→	// Flatten existing tree
   698→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   699→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   700→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten base tree: %w", err)
   701→	}
   702→
   703→	// Remove deleted files
   704→	for _, file := range deletedFiles {
   705→		delete(entries, file)
   706→	}
   707→
   708→	// Add/update modified files
   709→	for _, file := range modifiedFiles {
   710→		// Resolve path relative to repo root for filesystem operations
   711→		absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   712→		if !fileExists(absPath) {
   713→			delete(entries, file)
   714→			continue
   715→		}
   716→
   717→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(s.repo, absPath)
   718→		if err != nil {
   719→			// Skip files that can't be staged (may have been deleted since detection)
   720→			continue
   721→		}
   722→
   723→		entries[file] = object.TreeEntry{
   724→			Name: file,
   725→			Mode: mode,
   726→			Hash: blobHash,
   727→		}
   728→	}
   729→
   730→	// Add metadata directory files
   731→	if metadataDir != "" && metadataDirAbs != "" {
   732→		if err := addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(s.repo, metadataDirAbs, metadataDir, entries); err != nil {
   733→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to add metadata directory: %w", err)
   734→		}
   735→	}
   736→
   737→	// Build tree
   738→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   739→}

   741→// createCommit creates a commit object.
   742→func (s *GitStore) createCommit(treeHash, parentHash plumbing.Hash, message, authorName, authorEmail string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   743→	now := time.Now()
   744→	sig := object.Signature{
   745→		Name:  authorName,
   746→		Email: authorEmail,
