   514→// checkCanRewind checks if working directory is clean enough for rewind.
   515→// Returns (canRewind, reason, error). Shared by shadow and linear-shadow strategies.
   516→func checkCanRewind() (bool, string, error) {
   517→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   518→	if err != nil {
   519→		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   523→	if err != nil {
   524→		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
   525→	}
   526→
   527→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   528→	if err != nil {
   529→		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
   530→	}
   531→
   532→	if status.IsClean() {
   533→		return true, "", nil
   534→	}
   535→
   536→	var modified, added, deleted []string
   537→	for file, st := range status {
   538→		// Skip .entire directory
   539→		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(file) {
   540→			continue
   541→		}
   542→
   543→		// Skip untracked files
   544→		if st.Worktree == git.Untracked {
   545→			continue
   546→		}
   547→
   548→		switch {
   549→		case st.Staging == git.Added || st.Worktree == git.Added:
   550→			added = append(added, file)
   551→		case st.Staging == git.Deleted || st.Worktree == git.Deleted:
   552→			deleted = append(deleted, file)
   553→		case st.Staging == git.Modified || st.Worktree == git.Modified:
   554→			modified = append(modified, file)
   555→		}
   556→	}
   557→
   558→	if len(modified) == 0 && len(added) == 0 && len(deleted) == 0 {
   559→		return true, "", nil
   560→	}
   561→
   562→	var msg strings.Builder
   563→	msg.WriteString("You have uncommitted changes:\n")
   564→	for _, f := range modified {
   565→		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  modified:   %s\n", f))
   566→	}
   567→	for _, f := range added {
   568→		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  added:      %s\n", f))
   569→	}
   570→	for _, f := range deleted {
   571→		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  deleted:    %s\n", f))
   572→	}
   573→	msg.WriteString("\nPlease commit or stash your changes before rewinding.")
   574→
   575→	return false, msg.String(), nil
   576→}

   578→// checkCanRewindWithWarning checks working directory and returns a warning with diff stats.
   579→// Unlike checkCanRewind, this always returns canRewind=true but includes a warning message
   580→// with +/- line stats for uncommitted changes. Used by manual-commit strategy.
   581→func checkCanRewindWithWarning() (bool, string, error) {
   582→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   583→	if err != nil {
   584→		// Can't open repo - still allow rewind but without stats
   585→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if repo can't be opened
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   589→	if err != nil {
   590→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if worktree can't be accessed
   591→	}
   592→
   593→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   594→	if err != nil {
   595→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if status can't be retrieved
   596→	}
   597→
   598→	if status.IsClean() {
   599→		return true, "", nil
   600→	}
   601→
   602→	// Get HEAD commit tree for comparison - if we can't get it, just return without stats
   603→	head, err := repo.Head()
   604→	if err != nil {
   605→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even without HEAD (e.g., empty repo)
   606→	}
   607→
   608→	headCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   609→	if err != nil {
   610→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if commit lookup fails
   611→	}
   612→
   613→	headTree, err := headCommit.Tree()
   614→	if err != nil {
   615→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if tree lookup fails
   616→	}
   617→
   618→	type fileChange struct {
   619→		status   string // "modified", "added", "deleted"
   620→		added    int
   621→		removed  int
   622→		filename string
   623→	}
   624→
   625→	var changes []fileChange
   626→	// Use repo root, not cwd - git status returns paths relative to repo root
   627→	repoRoot, err := GetWorktreePath()
   628→	if err != nil {
   629→		return true, "", nil //nolint:nilerr // Rewind allowed even if repo root lookup fails
   630→	}
   631→
   632→	for file, st := range status {
   633→		// Skip .entire directory
   634→		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(file) {
   635→			continue
   636→		}
   637→
   638→		// Skip untracked files
   639→		if st.Worktree == git.Untracked {
   640→			continue
   641→		}
   642→
   643→		var change fileChange
   644→		change.filename = file
   645→
   646→		switch {
   647→		case st.Staging == git.Added || st.Worktree == git.Added:
   648→			change.status = "added"
   649→			// New file - count all lines as added
   650→			absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   651→			if content, err := os.ReadFile(absPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // absPath is repo root + relative path from git status
   652→				change.added = countLines(content)
   653→			}
   654→		case st.Staging == git.Deleted || st.Worktree == git.Deleted:
   655→			change.status = "deleted"
   656→			// Deleted file - count lines from HEAD as removed
   657→			if entry, err := headTree.File(file); err == nil {
   658→				if content, err := entry.Contents(); err == nil {
   659→					change.removed = countLines([]byte(content))
   660→				}
   661→			}
   662→		case st.Staging == git.Modified || st.Worktree == git.Modified:
   663→			change.status = "modified"
   664→			// Modified file - compute diff stats
   665→			var headContent, workContent []byte
   666→			if entry, err := headTree.File(file); err == nil {
   667→				if content, err := entry.Contents(); err == nil {
   668→					headContent = []byte(content)
   669→				}
   670→			}
   671→			absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   672→			if content, err := os.ReadFile(absPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // absPath is repo root + relative path from git status
   673→				workContent = content
   674→			}
   675→			if headContent != nil && workContent != nil {
   676→				change.added, change.removed = computeDiffStats(headContent, workContent)
   677→			}
   678→		default:
   679→			continue
   680→		}
   681→
   682→		changes = append(changes, change)
   683→	}
   684→
   685→	if len(changes) == 0 {
   686→		return true, "", nil
   687→	}
   688→
   689→	// Sort changes by filename for consistent output
   690→	sort.Slice(changes, func(i, j int) bool {
   691→		return changes[i].filename < changes[j].filename
   692→	})
   693→
   694→	var msg strings.Builder
   695→	msg.WriteString("The following uncommitted changes will be reverted:\n")
   696→
   697→	totalAdded, totalRemoved := 0, 0
   698→	for _, c := range changes {
   699→		totalAdded += c.added
   700→		totalRemoved += c.removed
   701→
   702→		var stats string
   703→		switch {
   704→		case c.added > 0 && c.removed > 0:
   705→			stats = fmt.Sprintf("+%d/-%d", c.added, c.removed)
   706→		case c.added > 0:
   707→			stats = fmt.Sprintf("+%d", c.added)
   708→		case c.removed > 0:
   709→			stats = fmt.Sprintf("-%d", c.removed)
   710→		}
   711→
   712→		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %-10s %s", c.status+":", c.filename))
   713→		if stats != "" {
   714→			msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", stats))
   715→		}
   716→		msg.WriteString("\n")
   717→	}
   718→
   719→	if totalAdded > 0 || totalRemoved > 0 {
   720→		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("\nTotal: +%d/-%d lines\n", totalAdded, totalRemoved))
   721→	}
   722→
   723→	return true, msg.String(), nil
   724→}

   726→// countLines counts the number of lines in content.
   727→func countLines(content []byte) int {
   728→	if len(content) == 0 {
   729→		return 0
   730→	}
   731→	count := 1
   732→	for _, b := range content {
   733→		if b == '\n' {
   734→			count++
   735→		}
   736→	}
   737→	// Don't count trailing newline as extra line
   738→	if len(content) > 0 && content[len(content)-1] == '\n' {
   739→		count--
   740→	}
   741→	return count
   742→}
   743→
   744→// computeDiffStats computes added and removed line counts between old and new content.
   745→// Uses a simple line-based diff algorithm.
   746→func computeDiffStats(oldContent, newContent []byte) (added, removed int) {
   747→	oldLines := splitLines(oldContent)
   748→	newLines := splitLines(newContent)
   749→
   750→	// Build a set of old lines with counts
   751→	oldSet := make(map[string]int)
   752→	for _, line := range oldLines {
   753→		oldSet[line]++
   754→	}
   755→
   756→	// Check which new lines are truly new
   757→	for _, line := range newLines {
   758→		if oldSet[line] > 0 {
   759→			oldSet[line]--
   760→		} else {
   761→			added++
   762→		}
   763→	}
   764→
   765→	// Remaining old lines are removed
   766→	for _, count := range oldSet {
   767→		removed += count
   768→	}
   769→
   770→	return added, removed
   771→}
   772→
   773→// splitLines splits content into lines, preserving empty lines.
   774→func splitLines(content []byte) []string {
   775→	if len(content) == 0 {
   776→		return nil
   777→	}
   778→	s := string(content)
   779→	// Remove trailing newline to avoid empty last element
   780→	s = strings.TrimSuffix(s, "\n")
   781→	return strings.Split(s, "\n")
   782→}

   791→type StageFilesContext string
   792→
   793→const (

   800→// StageFiles stages modified, new, and deleted files to the git worktree.
   801→//
   802→// This function handles three categories of file changes:
   803→//  1. Modified files: existing files that have been changed
   804→//  2. New files: files that were created during the session
   805→//  3. Deleted files: files that were removed during the session
   806→//
   807→// Error Handling Strategy:
   808→//   - Individual file staging errors are logged to stderr but don't fail the operation
   809→//   - This ensures that partial staging succeeds even if some files have issues
   810→//   - If a modified file no longer exists, it's treated as a deletion
   811→//
   812→// The stageCtx parameter is used for user-facing messages to indicate whether
   813→// this is staging for a session checkpoint or a task checkpoint.
   814→func StageFiles(worktree *git.Worktree, modified, newFiles, deleted []string, stageCtx StageFilesContext) {
   815→	// Get repo root for resolving file paths
   816→	// This is critical because fileExists() uses os.Stat() which resolves relative to CWD,
   817→	// but worktree.Add/Remove resolve relative to repo root. If CWD != repo root,
   818→	// fileExists() could return false for existing files, causing worktree.Remove()
   819→	// to incorrectly delete them.
   820→	repoRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()
   821→
   822→	// Stage modified files
   823→	for _, file := range modified {
   824→		// Resolve path relative to repo root for existence check
   825→		absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   826→		if fileExists(absPath) {
   827→			if _, err := worktree.Add(file); err != nil {
   828→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Failed to stage %s: %v\n", file, err)
   829→			} else {
   830→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Staged: %s\n", file)
   831→			}
   832→		} else {
   833→			// File was deleted - stage the deletion
   834→			if _, err := worktree.Remove(file); err != nil {
   835→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  File not found or deleted: %s\n", file)
   836→			}
   837→		}
   838→	}
   839→
   840→	// Stage new files
   841→	if len(newFiles) > 0 {
   842→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Staging %d new files created during %s:\n", len(newFiles), stageCtx)
   843→		for _, file := range newFiles {
   844→			if _, err := worktree.Add(file); err != nil {
   845→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Failed to stage %s: %v\n", file, err)
   846→			} else {
   847→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Staged new file: %s\n", file)
   848→			}
   849→		}
   850→	}
   851→
   852→	// Stage deleted files
   853→	for _, file := range deleted {
   854→		if _, err := worktree.Remove(file); err != nil {
   855→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Failed to stage deleted file %s: %v\n", file, err)
   856→		} else {
   857→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Staged deleted file: %s\n", file)
   858→		}
   859→	}
   860→}

   961→// collectUntrackedFiles collects all untracked files in the working directory.
   962→// This is used to capture the initial state when starting a session,
   963→// ensuring untracked files present at session start are preserved during rewind.
   964→// Excludes .git/, .entire/, and .claude/ directories (which are system/config directories).
   965→// Works correctly from any subdirectory within the repository.
   966→func collectUntrackedFiles() ([]string, error) {
   967→	// Get repository root to walk from there
   968→	repoRoot, err := GetWorktreePath()
   969→	if err != nil {
   970→		repoRoot = "." // Fallback to current directory
   971→	}
   972→
   973→	var untrackedFiles []string
   974→	err = filepath.Walk(repoRoot, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, walkErr error) error {
   975→		if walkErr != nil {
   976→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Skip filesystem errors during walk
   977→		}
   978→
   979→		// Get path relative to repo root
   980→		relPath, err := filepath.Rel(repoRoot, path)
   981→		if err != nil {
   982→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Skip paths we can't make relative
   983→		}
   984→
   985→		// Skip directories
   986→		if info.IsDir() {
   987→			// Skip .git, .claude, and .entire directories
   988→			if relPath == gitDir || relPath == claudeDir || relPath == entireDir ||
   989→				strings.HasPrefix(relPath, gitDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, claudeDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, entireDir+"/") {
   990→				return filepath.SkipDir
   991→			}
   992→			return nil
   993→		}
   994→
   995→		// Skip files in special directories (shouldn't reach here due to SkipDir, but safety check)
   996→		if strings.HasPrefix(relPath, gitDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, claudeDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, entireDir+"/") {
   997→			return nil
   998→		}
   999→
  1000→		untrackedFiles = append(untrackedFiles, relPath)
  1001→		return nil
  1002→	})
  1003→	if err != nil {
  1004→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to walk directory: %w", err)
  1005→	}
  1006→
  1007→	return untrackedFiles, nil
  1008→}

  1010→// ExtractSessionIDFromCommit extracts the session ID from a commit's trailers.
  1011→// It checks the Entire-Session trailer first, then falls back to extracting from
  1012→// the metadata directory path in the Entire-Metadata trailer.
  1013→// Returns empty string if no session ID is found.
  1014→func ExtractSessionIDFromCommit(commit *object.Commit) string {
  1015→	// Try Entire-Session trailer first
  1016→	if sessionID, found := trailers.ParseSession(commit.Message); found {
  1017→		return sessionID
  1018→	}
  1019→
  1020→	// Try extracting from metadata directory (last path component)
  1021→	if metadataDir, found := trailers.ParseMetadata(commit.Message); found {
  1022→		return filepath.Base(metadataDir)
  1023→	}
  1024→
  1025→	return ""
  1026→}

  1037→// createCommit creates a commit object
  1038→func createCommit(repo *git.Repository, treeHash, parentHash plumbing.Hash, message, authorName, authorEmail string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
  1039→	now := time.Now()
  1040→	sig := object.Signature{
  1041→		Name:  authorName,
  1042→		Email: authorEmail,
  1043→		When:  now,
  1044→	}
  1045→
  1046→	commit := &object.Commit{
  1047→		TreeHash:  treeHash,
  1048→		Author:    sig,
  1049→		Committer: sig,
  1050→		Message:   message,
  1051→	}
  1052→
